content: Valganciclovir is an antiviral medication that is converted in the body to its active form, ganciclovir. It is primarily used to prevent diseases caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) in individuals who have undergone organ transplants. CMV infections can lead to severe complications, including CMV retinitis, an eye infection that may result in blindness. Valganciclovir works by inhibiting the replication of the CMV virus. Additionally, it is used to treat CMV retinitis in patients with advanced HIV disease (AIDS). However, it is important to note that valganciclovir does not cure CMV disease, and in some cases, CMV retinitis may worsen despite treatment. Before starting valganciclovir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally with food as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. Swallow the tablets whole. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using the provided measuring device. Wash your hands thoroughly after handling this medication. Avoid contact with broken or crushed tablets, the liquid form, or the dust from the tablets on your skin, mucous membranes, or eyes. If accidental contact occurs, wash the area thoroughly with soap and water. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition. For children, the dosage is also based on body size. To ensure the medication works effectively, maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body by taking it at evenly spaced intervals. Do not change your dose or stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor. Do not substitute ganciclovir for valganciclovir without medical advice. Common side effects may include diarrhea, upset stomach, dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness, or tremors. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to valganciclovir are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing or passing out, seek emergency medical attention immediately. Before taking valganciclovir, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, ganciclovir, acyclovir, or any other substances. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Valganciclovir may cause dizziness or drowsiness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Valganciclovir can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious illnesses, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are taking valganciclovir before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. During pregnancy, valganciclovir should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. To prevent pregnancy, men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. Women of childbearing age should use reliable birth control methods (e.g., birth control pills and condoms) during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping the medication. It is unknown if valganciclovir passes into breast milk, but due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications, such as cancer chemotherapy, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, zidovudine, or cyclosporine, may decrease bone marrow function, lower blood cell counts, or cause kidney problems. Valganciclovir is very similar to ganciclovir, so do not use ganciclovir while taking valganciclovir unless directed by your doctor. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as difficulty breathing or loss of consciousness, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function tests, eye exams) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Store the liquid form in the refrigerator, but do not freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for disposal instructions. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
